title: Seven sorrows
hook: the prophecy, the flight, the loss, the road, the cross, the pietà, the tomb
carry: a sword shall pierce thy soul

segments.voice: Yesterday, Theotokos, Mother of God, and torches in the streets of Ephesus. Your line was a claim about her son. Did you pray the Hail Mary slowly, or hear it? Day eighty-one.

Forty days after Jesus is born, Mary and Joseph carry him into the temple in Jerusalem. It's a happy, ordinary visit, the kind new parents made. An old man named Simeon, who has waited his whole life for this, takes the baby in his arms and blesses God. Then he turns to Mary and says something no new mother wants to hear. In the Douay-Rheims: "And thy own soul a sword shall pierce, that, out of many hearts, thoughts may be revealed." Imagine walking home with that. Catholics have spent centuries sitting with what that sword turned out to be. Today: the seven sorrows of Mary.
screen: `FORTY DAYS OLD, IN THE TEMPLE.` → `AN OLD MAN, SIMEON.` → `A SWORD SHALL PIERCE.`

segments.voice: Tradition counts seven. The first is that prophecy itself. The second, the flight into Egypt: fleeing at night with a newborn, refugees, because a king wants him dead. The third, losing him. Jesus is twelve, and on the way home from Jerusalem they realize he's not in the group. Three days of searching. When they find him in the temple, Mary says: "Son, why hast thou done so to us? behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Every parent who has lost a child in a store for three minutes knows that voice. The fourth, meeting him on the road to the cross. The Gospels don't describe that moment. It comes from tradition and the Stations of the Cross. The fifth, standing at the cross. The sixth, holding his body when it's taken down. Artists call that the pietà, which means pity or devotion. Michelangelo carved the most famous one when he was in his early twenties, and it's the only work he ever signed. The seventh, the tomb: laying him in the rock and walking away. Five of the seven come from the Gospels. Two come from centuries of prayer. A religious order called the Servants of Mary, founded in Florence in the 1200s, spread this devotion, and the Church keeps the feast of Our Lady of Sorrows on September fifteenth, the day after the feast of the Cross. Here's why Catholics love it. It says Mary's faith wasn't a shield against grief. She wasn't spared. She was pierced, seven times, and stayed.
screen: `THE PROPHECY, THE FLIGHT, THE LOSS.` · `THE ROAD, THE CROSS.` · `THE PIETÀ, THE TOMB.` · `FAITH ISN'T A SHIELD AGAINST GRIEF.` · then, large: `THY OWN SOUL A SWORD SHALL PIERCE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold one sorrow gently. Settle and breathe. Let one sorrow of your own come to mind, big or small, old or new. Don't try to solve it or talk yourself out of it. Just hold it, the way you'd hold something fragile in both hands. Mary didn't make her sorrows go away. She kept them, and kept going. If you pray, you can hand this one to her, and ask her to hold it with you. The bell holds the time.
Seven sorrows. The prophecy, the flight, the loss, the road, the cross, the pietà, the tomb: Mary's grief, counted and kept. Today's word.
Your line: a sword shall pierce thy soul. Today, be gentle with someone who is grieving, even if the grief is old. Day eighty-one.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the memorial of Our Lady of Sorrows on 15 September, and some pray the chaplet of the seven sorrows, meditating on each one with a short set of prayers.

what it means: tradition counts seven sorrows, from Simeon's prophecy to the tomb, and says her faith wasn't a shield: she was pierced, and stayed.
what a scholar hears: five sorrows from the Gospels, two from tradition. the Servite order spread it from 1200s Florence, which is why art shows her heart pierced by seven swords.

notes: Douay-Rheims wording of Luke 2:35 and 2:48 given from memory; confirm.

The carry 'a sword shall pierce thy soul' is the index wording, not the Douay-Rheims word order ('thy own soul a sword shall pierce'). The script quotes the DR in the hook and teach and keeps the carry exact. Keeper may want the index line adjusted.

Five from the Gospels: prophecy (Luke), flight (Matthew), loss (Luke), cross (John), burial (the Gospels, with Mary's presence inferred from 'the women'); the descent from the cross into her arms and the meeting on the road are traditional. The script says 'five of the seven come from the Gospels'. Confirm the count is fair, since Mary's presence at the burial is not explicit.
Michelangelo's Pietà: completed c. 1499, when he was about 24; the only work he signed (on the sash). Confirm.
Servite Order founded c. 1233 in Florence by seven founders. Our Lady of Sorrows, 15 September (the day after the Exaltation of the Holy Cross). Confirm.
